q0878: Traveling user on untrusted Wi-Fi needs internal resources = VPN.
q0879: An IPS detects attacks by inspecting packets, so set up packet inspection first; logging comes after.
q0880: Remote users + inline URL reputation/category checks without backhauling traffic = SASE.
q0881: Protection that travels with the device on any network = host-based (HIPS, EDR, host firewall).
q0882: Traffic metadata between internal systems (who talked to whom, how much) = NetFlow.
q0883: Stop a malicious download or execution on the laptop itself = EDR.
q0884: Evaluating a vendor's security → ask for independent evidence: a third-party audit (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001).
q0885: Hashing = a one-way math function turning each password into a fixed digest.
q0886: Modifying the phone's system files to get admin/root = jailbreaking or rooting.
q0887: Evaluating a SaaS vendor's security → third-party audit report (SOC 2). An SLA only covers uptime.
q0888: Easy attack with free tools (ARP poisoning) for disruption's sake, at a school = unskilled attacker.
q0889: Harden a container image: strip what isn't needed (default apps) and disable insecure services (Telnet).
q0890: Validate a patch or fix = rescan.
q0891: Run a suspicious file safely to watch its behavior = sandbox.
q0892: OR 1=1 in a query = SQL injection. ../ = directory traversal. cat /etc/shadow = command injection.
q0893: Malicious insiders with valid access → UBA/UEBA spots behavior that departs from the baseline.
q0894: First policy slip after onboarding → focused retraining, not termination.
q0895: Old leaked password still worked → password history/reuse rules (plus regular changes) would have killed it.
q0896: Users reached a new malicious domain → update the proxy/web filter to block it.
q0897: Can reproduce the error and know source + destination → packet capture to see what happens on the wire.
q0898: Too much traffic to web servers → the load balancer logs show every request in front of them.
q0899: Deliberate PII misuse by an employee → privacy law and company compliance training.
q0900: Get a provider to erase your personal data = right to be forgotten. Closing the account isn't enough.
q0901: Block known-bad domains = DNS filtering. Inspect HTTPS content = TLS inspection proxy.
q0902: Text message leading to a fake login page = smishing.
q0903: Group running repeated ransomware for maximum profit = organized crime.
q0904: Breaking your own company's policy = internal non-compliance. Breaking a law or contract = external.
q0905: Software a company built and owns = intellectual property.
q0906: No network connection to the outside at all = air gap.
q0907: How long equipment runs before it fails = MTBF (drives maintenance). MTTR = time to fix.
